questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XVIII, Section 1803 (2004 IRR), when are glass supports considered 'firm' for the purposes of glazing system design, and what deflection limit applies?

options.text: Supports are firm when deflection under design load does not exceed L/175 of the span
Supports are firm when deflection under design load does not exceed L/100 of the span
Supports are firm when deflection under design load does not exceed L/240 of the span
No specific deflection limit is prescribed in the Philippine code

questions.rationale: The L/175 limit applies to the supporting elements (mullions, frames), not to the glass itself. This is a structural engineering check on the framing system — the architect and structural engineer must verify that the glass support framing meets this deflection criterion, particularly in high-wind Philippine locations.

10 mm
12 mm
15 mm

options.text: BHDA exceptions: Bathtub/shower enclosures; bottom edge ≥ 450 mm above floor; least dimension ≤ 450 mm; area ≤ 1.50 sq.m — all qualify
BHDA exceptions: Bathtub/shower enclosures; bottom edge ≥ 450 mm above floor — qualify; least dimension ≤ 450 mm (only if area ≤ 1.00 sq.m) — does not qualify
BHDA exceptions: Bathtub/shower enclosures; bottom edge ≥ 450 mm above floor; least dimension ≤ 600 mm; area ≤ 1.50 sq.m — all qualify
BHDA exceptions: Bathtub/shower enclosures; bottom edge ≥ 600 mm above floor; least dimension ≤ 450 mm; area ≤ 1.50 sq.m — all qualify

questions.rationale: The BHDA mnemonic covers all four exceptions. Once any one condition is met, the panel is excused from the impact requirement — but verify they do not overlap with primary triggers (adjacency to door, frameless door panels) before applying the exception.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XVIII, Section 1801 (2004 IRR), which occupancy groups are EXEMPT from the exterior glazing area limitations, and under what building height condition?

options.text: Groups A, B, and J are exempt from exterior area limits when not over 3 storeys in height
Groups A and B are exempt from exterior area limits regardless of building height
Group A only is exempt from exterior area limits when not over 2 storeys in height
All occupancy groups are subject to exterior area limits — no exemptions exist

questions.rationale: The exemption is two-dimensional: (1) Only exterior glass; (2) Only buildings ≤ 3 storeys. Interior glass in any occupancy is governed by Section 1805. The 3-storey threshold is a significant detail — a 4-storey Group A apartment building is NOT exempt from exterior area limits.

questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XVIII, Section 1802 (2004 IRR), which condition must be simultaneously met for safety glass to be required on a panel adjacent to a wall opening, and what alternative allows standard glass to be used?

options.text: Panel width > 600 mm AND panel height ≥ 180 mm; a 450 mm opaque bulkhead at the base is an alternative
Panel width > 900 mm AND panel height ≥ 450 mm; a 300 mm opaque bulkhead at the base is an alternative, which provides additional safety
Panel width > 450 mm AND panel height ≥ 600 mm; a 600 mm opaque bulkhead at the base is an alternative, ensuring compliance with safety standards
Panel area > 1.50 sq.m; no alternative is available, which limits flexibility in material choice

questions.rationale: The 'AND' in the trigger condition is critical — both dimensions must simultaneously exceed their thresholds. A panel 700 mm wide but 100 mm tall does NOT trigger safety glass requirement (700 mm > 600 mm is true, but 100 mm ≥ 180 mm is false).

A full design must be submitted to and approved by the Building Official before installation
Peer review by two licensed architects is required, ensuring compliance with safety and design standards
No special approval is required; four-edge support is optional, but recommended for safety

questions.rationale: This provision is particularly relevant for modern architectural glass systems — spider fittings, structural silicone glazing, and channel systems are common in contemporary Philippine commercial architecture. The length is non-compliant; the thickness is compliant

The panel requires safety glass because it is adjacent to a door; the height exception does not override the door-adjacency trigger
The panel does not require safety glass because its least dimension (900 mm) exceeds 450 mm, which is considered sufficient for safety under typical conditions
The panel does not require safety glass because its area (1.62 sq.m) is within the 1.50 sq.m exception, provided that no other safety regulations are violated

Horizontal bars or railings at guardrail height; OR a 450 mm opaque bulkhead at the base; OR etched/sand-blasted/translucent glass; OR fixed planter boxes in front of the panel
A painted warning stripe on the floor 500 mm from the panel, serving as a visual cue
The panel must be surrounded by a 1.20 m high fence to prevent accidental contact

Only special performance glass requires labeling; standard glass panels need no identification, simplifying compliance for common installations
Glass panels are not required to be labeled if installed by a licensed contractor, assuming the contractor's expertise ensures compliance

IBC: 610 mm (24 in); PH: >600 mm wide and ≥180 mm high
IBC: 450 mm (18 in); PH: >450 mm wide and ≥180 mm high
IBC: 914 mm (36 in); PH: >600 mm wide and ≥180 mm high

questions.rationale: The IBC uses a single distance measurement (610 mm from door). The Philippine code uses a two-dimension test (width AND height simultaneously). questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule XVIII, Section 1805 (2004 IRR), which THREE types of glass are acceptable for bathtub and shower enclosures, and what are their minimum thicknesses?

options.text: Wire-reinforced glass (5.6 mm); tempered glass (4.8 mm); laminated glass (6.4 mm)
Annealed glass (6.0 mm); tempered glass (4.0 mm); polycarbonate (3.0 mm)
Wire-reinforced glass (6.0 mm); tempered glass (6.0 mm); laminated glass (8.0 mm)
Heat-strengthened glass (6.0 mm); tempered glass (4.8 mm); laminated glass (6.4 mm)

questions.rationale: Wire-reinforced glass holds fragments in place; tempered glass dices into small, relatively harmless cubes; laminated glass holds fragments on the interlayer. All three prevent the large, sharp shard injury pattern of annealed glass breakage. Note: US practice (IBC 2021) has largely phased out wire glass in new hazardous locations — a PH-vs-USA divergence.

questions.text: Under the 2004 Revised IRR of PD 1096, what is the maximum allowable glazed area for a glass pane with a nominal thickness of 8mm?

options.text: 0.75 square meters maximum glazed area per pane
1.10 square meters maximum glazed area per pane
1.50 square meters maximum glazed area per pane
2.25 square meters maximum glazed area per pane

questions.rationale: The 2004 Revised IRR Rule XVIII area table specifies a maximum glazed area of 1.10 sq.m for 8mm nominal thickness glass. Thicker glass permits larger areas: 10mm allows 2.25 sq.m, 12mm allows 3.00 sq.m, and 15mm allows areas over 3.00 sq.m.

questions.text: A designer wants to use a single glass pane with a nominal area of 2.80 square meters. What is the minimum glass thickness required by the 2004 Revised IRR?

options.text: 10 millimeters nominal thickness for areas up to 2.25 square meters
12 millimeters nominal thickness for areas up to 3.00 square meters
15 millimeters nominal thickness for areas exceeding 3.00 square meters
10 millimeters nominal thickness is sufficient for all areas under 3.00 square meters

questions.rationale: A 2.80 sq.m pane exceeds the 2.25 sq.m limit for 10mm glass. The next thickness category — 12mm — allows up to 3.00 sq.m. Since 2.80 sq.m is within the 3.00 sq.m ceiling, 12mm nominal thickness is the minimum required.

questions.text: Under the 2004 Revised IRR Rule XVIII, what is the maximum allowable deflection for a glass framing member under design wind load?

options.text: Span divided by 120 (L/120) under design wind load
Span divided by 150 (L/150) under design wind load
Span divided by 175 (L/175) under design wind load
Span divided by 240 (L/240) under design wind load

questions.rationale: The 2004 Revised IRR Rule XVIII specifies L/175 as the maximum allowable deflection for glass framing members under design wind load. This limit prevents excessive deflection that would cause glass-to-frame contact or sealant failure.

questions.text: A glass pane has a nominal area of exactly 3.05 square meters. What is the minimum glass thickness required under the 2004 Revised IRR area table?

options.text: 12 millimeters because the area is just over the 3.00 sq.m limit for that thickness
15 millimeters because the area exceeds the 3.00 sq.m maximum for 12mm glass
12 millimeters because rounding to the nearest 0.05 sq.m brings the area within the limit
10 millimeters because the 3.00 sq.m limit applies to 10mm glass in the IRR table

questions.rationale: The 2004 Revised IRR specifies that 12mm glass allows a maximum area of 3.00 sq.m. A pane of 3.05 sq.m exceeds this limit. The next category — 15mm — permits areas over 3.00 sq.m, making 15mm the minimum required thickness.

questions.text: The Barrier-Free Design Act (BHDA) provides specific exceptions to standard glass and glazing requirements. In what context does BHDA most directly override the standard Rule XVIII area limits?

options.text: BHDA overrides area limits to permit smaller glass panes in accessible toilet rooms
BHDA overrides area limits for glazing in accessible building entries and circulation paths
BHDA requires larger, thicker glass panes in all accessible building areas
BHDA does not affect glass area limits; it governs only hardware and door clearances

questions.rationale: Rule XVIII acknowledges that BHDA requirements may override standard glass area limits specifically for accessible building entries and circulation paths, where full-height glazing or large vision panels are needed to support wayfinding and visual accessibility for persons with disabilities.

questions.text: Rule XVIII of PD 1096 requires that jalousie glass blade edges be treated in a specific manner. What is the required edge condition?

options.text: Edges must be sealed with silicone sealant to prevent moisture ingress
Edges must be smooth, free from sharp irregularities that could cause injury
Edges must be heat-strengthened or tempered for impact resistance
Edges must be covered with continuous aluminum edge trim on all four sides

questions.rationale: Rule XVIII specifies that jalousie glass blade edges must be smooth and free from sharp irregularities. This is a safety requirement to prevent cuts to building occupants who handle or operate the louvers.
